title: Recursion, and converting recursion to iteration

claims.text: Turing’s 1946 report describes the mechanism for subsidiary operations as noting where the major operation left off and, on completion, consulting a list of such notes held with the most recent last — which in modern terms is a stack of return addresses.

source.title: Turing, A. M., Proposals for the development in the Mathematics Division of an Automatic Computing Engine (ACE), Report E882, National Physical Laboratory, February 1946

claims.text: Tarjan’s 1972 paper treats depth-first search and backtracking as the same technique, and its listed key words include both backtracking and depth-first.

source.title: Tarjan, R., Depth-First Search and Linear Graph Algorithms, SIAM Journal on Computing 1(2):146-160, June 1972

beats.broke: recursion spends a resource the program never mentions, in an amount set by the input, so a correct function fails on data that is merely deep
beats.fix: make the hidden stack explicit — push the state the recursion would have kept in local variables, and loop while it is non-empty
beats.cost: the transformation is mechanical only once you have identified every value that survived across the recursive call, and that set is larger than it looks
beats.interview: what exactly has to go into the explicit stack
